notebooks.title: Refined Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds and Finite Relaxation
notebooks.summary: Coarse-graining and finite relaxation times establish strict lower bounds on observable entropy production and link computational accuracy to thermodynamic dissipation.
notebooks.findings:
Coarse-graining of microscopic degrees of freedom implies that only a lower bound on entropy production can be retrieved from coarse-grained data. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

For reversible continuous-time Markov networks, computational error admits a universal thermodynamic bound relating lag error to entropy production rate and memory time. [source-7be42e4ac5ea4936]
notebooks.limitations: Findings rely on theoretical continuous-time Markovian network models and coarse-grained effective descriptions.
notebooks.next_questions: How do nonreciprocal couplings modify these thermodynamic bounds in autonomous quantum information engines?
notebooks.reason: Revising notebook to incorporate rigorous coarse-graining limits and thermodynamic bounds on computational error.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory States
notebooks.summary: Information engines require distinct, multiple memory states to effectively leverage temporal correlations in inputs, imposing fundamental thermodynamic costs.
notebooks.findings: An information engine must possess more than one memory state to leverage correlations between input environment fluctuations and work production. [source-f86c77845cb8449d]

detail.title: Refined Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds and Finite Relaxation
detail.summary: Coarse-graining and finite relaxation times establish strict lower bounds on observable entropy production and link computational accuracy to thermodynamic dissipation.
detail.findings:
Coarse-graining of microscopic degrees of freedom implies that only a lower bound on entropy production can be retrieved from coarse-grained data. [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

For reversible continuous-time Markov networks, computational error admits a universal thermodynamic bound relating lag error to entropy production rate and memory time. [source-7be42e4ac5ea4936]
detail.limitations: Findings rely on theoretical continuous-time Markovian network models and coarse-grained effective descriptions.
detail.next_questions: How do nonreciprocal couplings modify these thermodynamic bounds in autonomous quantum information engines?
detail.reason: Revising notebook to incorporate rigorous coarse-graining limits and thermodynamic bounds on computational error.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory States
detail.summary: Information engines require distinct, multiple memory states to effectively leverage temporal correlations in inputs, imposing fundamental thermodynamic costs.
detail.findings: An information engine must possess more than one memory state to leverage correlations between input environment fluctuations and work production. [source-f86c77845cb8449d]
detail.limitations: The relationship between state count and dissipation relies on idealized engines; hardware-specific overheads (e.g., refresh energy) are not fully integrated.
detail.next_questions: Can the thermodynamic cost of state retention be mapped to specific epsilon-machine complexity measures?
detail.reason: Synthesizing thermodynamic costs and information engine mechanics using existing evidence.
